title: India DPDP readiness checklist
legal_review_status: Plain-language aid prepared from the official texts. Not reviewed by counsel and not legal advice. Have a qualified professional confirm applicability and wording before relying on any item as an obligation for your organisation.
effective_status_note: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025 commence in phases under the MeitY commencement notification of November 2025. Confirm whether a provision is in force on your assessment date; this checklist records readiness, not a current legal duty.

controls.title: Notice to the people whose data you process
controls.question: Do you collect personal data from individuals that is used to build, test or run this AI system?
controls.requirement: People are told what personal data is processed, for what purpose, how to exercise their rights and how to complain.
required_evidence: Copy of the notice shown to individuals
Where and when it is shown
controls.guidance: A short, plain notice linked from the point of data collection is the usual starting evidence.

controls.title: Lawful ground: consent or a specified legitimate use
controls.question: For each purpose this system serves, which ground applies: consent, or a legitimate use listed in the Act?
controls.requirement: Each purpose has a documented ground. Consent, where relied on, is specific and can be withdrawn.
controls.guidance: Do not assume consent is needed for everything, and do not assume a legitimate use applies without checking the Act.

controls.title: Only the data needed for the stated purpose
controls.question: Does the model or the audit data include personal fields that are not needed for the purpose?
controls.requirement: Personal data processed is limited to what is necessary for the specified purpose.
required_evidence: Data inventory with purpose for each personal field
Justification for personal fields used as model inputs
controls.guidance: The automatic privacy scan lists candidate personal-data columns. Use it to prepare this justification.

controls.title: Accuracy and completeness where data drives decisions
controls.question: Is personal data used to make a decision that affects a person?
controls.requirement: Reasonable efforts are made to keep personal data complete, accurate and consistent when it is used to make a decision affecting the person.
controls.guidance: Drift and missing-data results from the audit can support this item.
controls.not_applicable_reason: The system was not marked as making or driving decisions about people.

controls.title: Reasonable security safeguards
controls.source: DPDP Act 2023, s.8; DPDP Rules 2025, r.6
controls.question: What technical and organisational safeguards protect the personal data used here (access control, encryption, logging, backups)?
controls.requirement: Reasonable security safeguards protect personal data against breach.
controls.guidance: This tool cannot verify your infrastructure. Upload what you have and have a reviewer judge adequacy.

controls.title: Personal data breach response
controls.source: DPDP Act 2023, s.8; DPDP Rules 2025, r.7
controls.question: Is there a written procedure to detect, contain and report a personal data breach, with a named owner?
controls.requirement: A breach can be detected and reported to the Board and affected people as required.
required_evidence: Date of last test or review
controls.guidance: A missing procedure is a common early gap. Check the Rules for the report content and timelines.

controls.title: Retention and erasure
controls.question: Do you have a retention period for this data and a way to delete it when it is no longer needed?
controls.requirement: Personal data is erased when its purpose is served or consent is withdrawn, unless law requires retention.
required_evidence: Evidence a deletion has been carried out
controls.guidance: The audit can count rows past a declared retention date. The schedule and deletion proof come from you.

controls.title: Processors acting on your behalf
controls.question: Do vendors or cloud services process this personal data for you?
controls.requirement: Processing by others is under a valid contract, and you remain responsible for it.
controls.guidance: Include hosting, analytics and labelling vendors.

controls.title: Rights requests and grievance redressal
controls.question: Can a person ask what data you hold, correct it, have it erased, and complain, and who handles that?
controls.requirement: People have working routes to access, correction, erasure and grievance redressal, with published contact details.
required_evidence: Example of a handled request or a test
controls.guidance: For automated decisions, also record how a person can ask for a human to look at the outcome.

controls.title: Children's personal data
controls.question: Does the system process personal data of anyone under 18?
controls.requirement: Verifiable parental consent is obtained and tracking or targeted advertising directed at children is avoided, subject to exemptions.
required_evidence: Method used to establish age and parental consent
controls.guidance: Applies only if children's data is processed.
controls.not_applicable_reason: The system was not marked as processing children's data.

controls.title: Significant Data Fiduciary status
controls.source: DPDP Act 2023, s.10; DPDP Rules 2025, r.13
controls.question: Has the Central Government notified your organisation as a Significant Data Fiduciary?
controls.requirement: Additional duties apply only to notified Significant Data Fiduciaries. Most startups are not.
required_evidence: Statement of status with the basis for it
If notified: DPO appointment, independent data audit and impact assessment records
controls.guidance: Do not assume the extra duties apply to you. Do not assume they never will as you grow.
controls.not_applicable_reason: The system was not marked as run by a Significant Data Fiduciary.
